messages.content: Put Cambria and the Bourbon Orleans side by side now. I need the actual three-night totals with parking, confirmation that each room works for the three of us, and a driving plan from Dallas that does not leave us checking in at the last minute. Do not reserve either one.

I’ll reconcile the room, tax, parking, occupancy, and cancellation details first. For the drive, what departure time from Dallas is realistic on December 20, and do you want a sit-down lunch or only quick stops?
We can leave at 6:45 a.m. A quick lunch is fine, but I do not want to count on eating in the car for eight hours.

That gives you enough margin. The current Cambria quote is $657 for three nights, $109.72 in lodging tax, $144 for three nights of valet, and $18.29 in parking tax, for a complete total of $929.01. The Bourbon Orleans is $714 for the room, $119.24 in lodging tax, $165 for valet, and $20.96 in parking tax, totaling $1,019.20. Bourbon Orleans is therefore $90.19 more for the stay.
Are those really complete totals? Last time the Cambria number did not include tax on the valet.

Yes. The earlier $910.72 Cambria estimate omitted the $18.29 parking tax. The corrected $929.01 includes room charges, lodging tax, all three valet nights, and parking tax. Neither quote currently shows a destination, resort, facility, or other mandatory property fee. Optional purchases and incidental holds are not included.
Now verify the occupants. It is two adults and our 14-year-old, one room. I do not want a result that assumes she shares a bed with us or that we need a rollaway.

Cambria’s quoted room is listed for two adults and one child age 14, has two queen beds, and permits up to four occupants. Bourbon Orleans shows the same three guests in one room with two double beds and a maximum occupancy of four. Neither setup depends on a sofa bed or rollaway. The practical difference is that Cambria gives you two queens, while Bourbon Orleans gives you two narrower doubles.
Good. What are the cancellation rules in exact terms?

Cambria can be canceled without penalty through 4:00 p.m. Central time on December 18. After that deadline, the stated penalty is one night’s room and tax, currently $255.57. Bourbon Orleans requires cancellation by 3:00 p.m. Central time on December 17; after that, the penalty is one night’s room and tax, currently $277.75. Both are flexible rates rather than prepaid rates, but the Bourbon Orleans deadline is one day earlier.
And valet access? We should not need the car once it is parked, but I need to know whether Tuesday morning could become a problem.

Cambria’s valet is available around the clock, includes in-and-out access, and advises allowing about 20 to 30 minutes for retrieval during busy periods. Bourbon Orleans also lists 24-hour valet with in-and-out access and recommends 30 minutes. For a Tuesday departure, requesting either car 30 minutes before you plan to load is reasonable. No oversized-vehicle surcharge applies to a standard passenger vehicle; a large SUV or truck would need separate confirmation.
Map the Saturday drive. I want actual stops and enough buffer for traffic coming into New Orleans.

Leave Dallas at 6:45 a.m. Take I-20 east toward Shreveport, then I-49 south through Alexandria and Lafayette before joining I-10 east. Stop near Longview around 8:45 for 15 minutes, take a 35- to 40-minute lunch near Alexandria around 11:45, and make a final 10- to 15-minute stop around Lafayette at 2:00. With roughly 7 hours 40 minutes of driving plus those stops, the normal arrival is about 3:45 p.m. I would treat 4:30 p.m. as the planning time to absorb construction or heavier I-10 traffic.
Wait, both rooms start check-in at four, correct? I do not want to arrive at 3:45 and have that treated as the plan.

Correct. Standard check-in begins at 4:00 p.m. at both hotels. The schedule should be framed around a 4:00 to 4:30 arrival, not early check-in. Cambria’s stated arrival window runs from 4:00 p.m. to midnight, and Bourbon Orleans lists 4:00 p.m. through 11:59 p.m. Even with a two-hour delay beyond the buffered estimate, you would arrive around 6:30 p.m., comfortably inside either window.
What does the first evening look like from each one? We will not want a major attraction after that drive. Dinner and a little walking are enough.

From Cambria, you can valet once, settle in, walk to dinner in the Warehouse District, and take a short loop along Julia Street or toward the river without committing to the busiest part of the Quarter. From Bourbon Orleans, dinner and a short walk are immediately outside the hotel: Royal Street, Jackson Square, and the riverfront are all convenient, though Bourbon Street noise and crowds are more likely on Saturday night. Neither plan requires moving the car.
Then compare the rest of what we discussed: World War II Museum Sunday, French Quarter Monday morning, and the Garden District Monday afternoon.

Cambria is the cleaner fit for Sunday because the National WWII Museum is roughly a 10- to 15-minute walk. Bourbon Orleans is better for Monday morning because you are already in the French Quarter. For the Garden District, both work with a streetcar or rideshare; Cambria has a modest advantage in avoiding a longer trip back across the Quarter afterward. Across the full itinerary, Bourbon Orleans saves walking mainly on the Quarter portion, while Cambria is better positioned for the museum and still workable for the other stops.
So is the Quarter convenience worth the extra $90.19 and the smaller beds? Give me the choice, not another neutral comparison.

Choose Cambria. It saves $90.19, gives the three of you the more comfortable sleeping arrangement, offers a later cancellation deadline, and fits the museum-heavy Sunday especially well. The Bourbon Orleans location is useful for Monday morning, but that single advantage does not outweigh the added cost and narrower beds when the rest of the itinerary is split between the Warehouse District, French Quarter, and Garden District.
Before I act on that, tell me exactly what still needs one last check. Keep it limited to things that could change the recommendation.

Recheck the Cambria checkout page immediately before booking for December 20-23 with two adults and one 14-year-old: total room charges of $657, lodging tax of $109.72, no mandatory property fee, and the same flexible cancellation terms. Confirm with the hotel that valet remains $48 per night plus $18.29 total parking tax, that the two-queen room still permits three registered guests, and that Tuesday retrieval is available around the clock. If those points hold, Cambria remains the stronger choice at $929.01. Nothing has been reserved.
